brief.greeting: Good morning. German AI folks finally let their model fly without a passport.

stories.headline: Aleph Alpha unveils sovereign Kolibri LLM
stories.body: **German‑first LLM launch:** Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, an open‑weight large language model built in Germany and now publicly available. The same team posted a technical report detailing the architecture and training data.
stories.why: You can experiment with a state‑of‑the‑art model without vendor lock‑in.

stories.headline: ESP32 doubles as a software‑defined radio
stories.body: **Tiny chip, big ears:** Hackaday shows the ESP32 can act as a standalone SDR receiver, pulling raw RF data without extra hardware. It runs the demodulation code directly on the microcontroller.
stories.why: Your next IoT project can listen to the airwaves without a pricey dongle.

stories.headline: FTL OS targets cloud‑scale workloads
stories.body: **New cloud OS released:** FTL, an operating system designed for cloud environments, is now open on GitHub. It promises lower latency and tighter resource isolation than traditional kernels.
stories.why: If you spin up VMs daily, a leaner OS could shave seconds off boot time.

highlights.title: Aleph Alpha Kolibri: How the sovereign German LLM works
highlights.summary: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri, a sovereign German open-weight large language model.
highlights.detail: The model is positioned as a European alternative to major US providers, emphasizing data sovereignty. It is available under an open-weight license, allowing users to run and modify the model locally. The announcement was shared via a Hacker News post linking to Aleph Alpha's blog.

highlights.title: The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed.
highlights.summary: A Hugging Face blog post discusses a mismatch between an agent's completion claim and the database state.
highlights.detail: The article highlights challenges in ensuring consistency between AI-generated actions and underlying data stores. It serves as a case study for debugging agent behavior in production pipelines. No specific model or version details are provided.

highlights.title: The ESP32, An SDR In Itself
highlights.summary: Hackaday reports that the ESP32 can function as a standalone software-defined radio receiver.
highlights.detail: Building on the legacy of the RTL-SDR, the ESP32 leverages its built-in radio capabilities to process RF signals without external hardware. The article suggests potential for compact, low-cost SDR projects, though implementation details are brief.

highlights.title: FTL: A new operating system for clouds
highlights.summary: FTL is a new operating system designed for cloud environments, with source code hosted on GitHub.
highlights.detail: The project targets scalable, container‑friendly workloads and aims to simplify resource management across distributed nodes. Early documentation outlines its microkernel architecture and API surface.

highlights.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
highlights.summary: Aleph Alpha published a technical report and additional paper on Kolibri, their sovereign open-weight model.
highlights.detail: The report, linked in the Hacker News post, provides architecture details, training data sources, and performance metrics. An accompanying blog post offers a higher-level overview. Both documents are publicly accessible for deeper technical insight.

items.title: Play PlayStation 2 and XBox 1 Games on Your Jailbroken PS5
items.summary: Hackaday explains how to run PlayStation 2 and Xbox 1 games on a jailbroken PlayStation 5.
items.detail: The guide notes that modern consoles like the PS5 are essentially x86 PCs with custom firmware, enabling compatibility layers for older console titles. It requires a jailbroken system and appropriate emulation software.

items.title: Seven stable kernels for Saturday
items.summary: Greg Kroah-Hartman released seven stable Linux kernel versions: 7.2.9, 6.18.55, 6.12.112, 6.6.158, 6.1.189, 5.15.222, and 5.10.271, each containing numerous important fixes.
items.detail: These updates span the current long‑term and stable branches, addressing security patches, driver regressions, and core subsystem bugs. Users of any of these kernels are encouraged to upgrade promptly to benefit from the cumulative fixes.

items.title: Zig 0.17 released
items.summary: Zig 0.17 was released after a five‑month cycle, incorporating contributions from 206 developers across 925 commits, with a reworked build system and an enhanced ELF linker targeting incremental compilation on x86_64‑linux.
items.detail: The new Build Server Protocol aims to streamline remote builds, while the linker improvements lay groundwork for full incremental compilation, a long‑requested feature. This release marks a substantial step beyond the originally planned short cycle.

items.title: 2026 Retrocomputer Challenge: Vectron65 Plus Puts the Emphasis on Plus
items.summary: The 2026 Retrocomputer Challenge highlights the Vectron65 Plus, a home computer built around a 6502 CPU with optional add‑on modules.
items.detail: Designer Nick Bild emphasizes modularity, allowing users to expand the system with additional peripherals. The project showcases the enduring appeal of classic 8‑bit architecture in modern hobbyist builds.

related.title: 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge: A Homebrew Computer In Only Three ICs

items.title: A Good DIY Solder Stencil Begins With a Cleanly-Sliced Soda Can
items.summary: A DIY solder stencil can be made by cleanly slicing a soda can, offering a low‑cost alternative to steel‑cut professional stencils.
items.detail: The method provides precise apertures for applying solder paste on small PCBs, making it popular among hobbyists who lack access to CNC‑cut tools. Proper cleaning and cutting are essential to avoid contamination.

items.detail: The project targets scalable, container‑friendly workloads and aims to simplify resource management across distributed nodes. Early documentation outlines its microkernel architecture and API surface.

items.title: kth-competitive-programming/kactl
items.summary: kth-competitive-programming/kactl is a C++ template library providing algorithms and data structures for competitive programming.
items.detail: Maintained by KTH participants, the library includes implementations for graph algorithms, geometry, and number theory, facilitating rapid solution development during contests.

items.title: agno-agi/agno
items.summary: agn0-agi/agno is a Python toolkit for building, executing, and managing agent platforms.
items.detail: The repository provides command‑line utilities and libraries to define agent workflows, handle state, and orchestrate multiple agents. It targets developers who need a lightweight framework for custom AI agent deployments.

items.title: arc53/DocsGPT
items.summary: arc53/DocsGPT is a private AI platform offering agent building, deep research, document analysis, multi‑model support, and API connectivity for enterprise search.
items.detail: Designed for secure environments, DocsGPT runs locally or within a private cloud, allowing organizations to integrate large language models without exposing data. It includes a visual builder for assembling agents that can query documents and external APIs.

items.title: calesthio/OpenMontage
items.summary: calesthio/OpenMontage is an open‑source, agentic video production system with 12 pipelines, over 100 tools, and 700+ agent skill files.
items.detail: The system lets developers script AI‑driven video creation, chaining agents that handle tasks like scripting, rendering, and editing. It aims to replace proprietary video pipelines by providing modular, reusable components.

items.title: cjpais/Handy
items.summary: cjpais/Handy is a free, offline‑only speech‑to‑text application written in Rust.
items.detail: Handy runs entirely on the user’s device, avoiding cloud services and preserving privacy. It supports extensible plugins for custom language models and can be integrated into other Rust projects.

items.title: cloudflare/cloudflare-os
items.summary: cloudflare/cloudflare-os provides an agent workspace built on Cloudflare Workers for document creation, app building, and running agents with company context.
items.detail: The platform leverages the edge‑computing capabilities of Cloudflare Workers to host lightweight agents that can access internal data stores and APIs, enabling rapid internal tool development.
